rationale: Greek loanword θρόνος. Both spellings appear on this page; line 12 ⲫⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ preserves the rho. Technical Manichaean cosmological term for the nine great thrones occupied by divine beings at successive cosmic levels (firmaments, air, ecclesia).

Standard Manichaean cosmological figure occupying the seventh firmament. ⲛⲁⲃ 'great' + ⲛ̄ⲣⲡⲟ 'of kings' + ⲧⲁⲓⲟ 'honor.' Greek source: μέγας βασιλεὺς τῆς τιμῆς. Distinguished from the King of Lights / Father of Greatness.

Greek κριτής + Coptic ⲙⲏⲉ 'truth.' Standard Manichaean cosmological figure stationed in the air who judges all souls and divides them onto three paths: death, life, and reconciliation/agreement. Distinct from the Apostle as Judge of Righteousness.

proposed_english: to wear / to clothe oneself in
rationale: Greek loanword φορεῖν 'to bear, to wear (a garment).' Used here for the Living Spirit's wearing of the three cosmological garments (wind, fire, water).
ϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ 'three' + ⲍⲃⲥⲱ 'garment' (= ϩⲃⲥⲱ). Manichaean technical triad: the wind-garment, the fire-garment, the water-garment of the Living Spirit. Title of this kephalaion (line 18).
Lyc ⲍⲏⲩ = Sah. ϩⲏⲩ 'naked.' With ⲕⲱⲕ 'strip' = 'strip bare, denude.' Used here of the wind-garment's action upon the cosmic subjects.
ⲡⲙⲏⲧ likely = ⲡⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'the midst' (with elision of final -ⲉ); + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Spatial-directional adverbial. Tentative.
ⲡⲍⲉⲡ = ϩⲁⲡ 'judgment, sentence' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲍⲉⲡⲡ tentative); ⲙⲙⲏⲉ 'of truth.' Standard collocation for the apostolic juridical pronouncement.
Verbal idiom ϯ- 'give' + ⲍⲉⲡ 'judgment' = 'render judgment.' The Judge of Truth is described as 'the one who gives judgment to all men.'
